title: APOE ε4 and late-onset Alzheimer disease risk: non-deterministic robust genetic-risk control
summary: Positive-control record for MKH-PAT-0015. APOE ε4 is encoded not as a deterministic diagnosis, but as a durable gene/risk relation that prevents the candidate-gene denominator pattern from becoming an anti-gene or all-candidates-fail rule.

status_history.note: Promoted after rev0018 explicitly called for candidate-gene success controls.

place.scope: late-onset Alzheimer disease genetic-risk evidence; individual medical interpretation excluded

claims.claim: MedlinePlus Genetics describes APOE as encoding apolipoprotein E, identifies e2/e3/e4 as major alleles, and states that APOE e4 increases risk for late-onset Alzheimer disease, with two inherited e4 copies conferring greater risk than one.
what_would_change_status: A corrected NIH/NLM page materially changes the allele/risk relation or removes the Alzheimer disease association.

claims.claim: The APOE control is explicitly non-deterministic: the source says people inherit increased risk, not the disease itself, and that not all people with Alzheimer disease have APOE e4 nor all people with APOE e4 develop the disease.
what_would_change_status: A stronger clinical-genetics guideline reclassifies APOE e4 as deterministic in the specific late-onset scope, or the source changes its risk/not-disease language.

claims.claim: As a pattern-control record, APOE ε4 shows that MKH-PAT-0015 must distinguish failed low-powered candidate literatures from durable gene/risk relations; it calibrates the pattern without making APOE a diagnosis, causal proof, or clinical-actionability claim.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass review finds APOE is a poor positive control because its discovery/evidence route is categorically unlike the candidate-gene literatures being calibrated.

evidence_refs.support_type: control role and scope encoded in this record

evidence_profile.why_control_not_case: It is not a negative result; it is a calibrator showing a robust, non-deterministic genetic-risk relation.

type_payload.fit_rationale: Robust gene/risk relation with explicit non-determinism; prevents anti-genetics overfit.
limits: Not a deterministic or diagnostic claim.
Does not by itself demonstrate GWAS causation or clinical actionability.
Ancestry and risk-modifier literature require second-pass review.

handling_notes: Genetic findings must not be represented as deterministic individual destiny.
No clinical advice, testing advice, or individual-level participant data is encoded.
Population/ancestry, phenotype, and actionability scope must remain visible.

unknowns: Whether APOE should be modeled as a candidate-gene success, a prior known-risk gene, or a separate robust-risk-gene control class.
How ancestry-specific risk modification should be represented in a later child record.
next_actions: Add a second-pass source record from a peer-reviewed APOE/GWAS review with page locators.
Add ancestry/diversity caveat child record before any mature pattern synthesis.

scope_qualifiers.ancestry_or_population_scope: ancestry and modifiers not second-pass reviewed
scope_qualifiers.portability_caution: risk allele is not deterministic or diagnostic
